R618.note: Adds secure:true to the cookie options, the textbook fix for CWE-614; no other behavior changed.

R619.note: Primary fix calls DocumentRepository.findById() and Document.getOwnerId(), neither of which exist anywhere in the given files (no ownership data model at all), so it would not compile/work against this codebase; it also returns 403, which reveals more than the contract's required not-found-equivalent response (the disclosed 'alternative' addresses this but isn't the implemented fix).

R620.note: os.Lstat + IsRegular() correctly rejects a planted symlink leaf while leaving normal file reads untouched.

R621.note: Adds an underflow-safe check that length <= receivedByteCount-2 before the memmove, closing the OOB read without altering the success path.

R622.note: Misdiagnoses the sink: there is no autoescape=False config anywhere in this file (it's a raw f-string return, no Jinja rendering at all); the actual injection point is `Markup(label)` wrapping unescaped user input, which the write-up never identifies or removes, so no real code change is given and the vulnerability remains open.

R623.note: Bounds check field_index >= MAX_FIELDS before the array read cleanly closes the OOB read; error path matches existing -1 convention.

R624.note: realpath() canonicalization plus base-directory prefix check correctly blocks traversal/symlink escape while preserving normal report downloads.

R625.note: Primary whitelist/host check correctly blocks redirects to non-whitelisted hosts (including protocol-relative //host, since URI parses a host from it); the listed 'alternative' (startsWith("/")) is flawed since it would also allow protocol-relative //evil.com, but that variant is not the one actually needed.

R626.note: Swapping to jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment is the standard mitigation for untrusted Jinja2 source and preserves the render_preview signature, autoescape setting, and context data unchanged.

R627.note: Ownership check uses real ClaimsPrincipal/record fields and compiles, but returns Forbid() (403) on mismatch, which the stated contract explicitly forbids ('should not reveal more than the original not-found path' i.e. 404); this deviation isn't flagged in the write-up.

R628.note: Allowlist mapping of the field parameter to fixed column names closes the identifier-injection vector while keeping term parameterized and approved fields working; unknown fields degrade to the default 'name' search rather than erroring, which is disclosed in the code and not harmful.

R629.note: shared_ptr<Observer> ties observer lifetime to subscription, the standard fix for this dangling-pointer pattern; the required call-site change (heap-allocate via make_shared) is stated plainly.

R630.note: Argument-list subprocess.run with shell=False removes shell interpretation; input_path is always prefixed with UPLOAD_DIR so a validated filename can't be read as a leading-dash flag, and the added allowlist regex is shown plainly.

R631.note: Switching to redis-py's hset() uses RESP length-prefixed encoding, eliminating CRLF/command injection via the inline protocol; the fallback hand-rolled RESP snippet is missing the required '*4\r\n' multibulk array header and would not actually work, but it's offered only as a secondary contingency, not the primary fix.

R632.note: Drops the attacker-controlled seed entirely and uses no-arg SecureRandom, the correct fix since accepting a client seed for a security token was itself the flaw; removal is stated openly.

R633.note: Primary suggested replacement (32 random bytes, base64 URL-safe) is an appropriately shaped secure token; the listed 'minimal' alternative (SecureRandom.nextDouble().substring) can yield very short/low-entropy strings for round values, but the stronger option is the one actually recommended.

R634.note: Argument-array subprocess.run with shell=False closes shell metacharacter injection, but target_host is passed unguarded as a bare argument to ping with no leading-dash rejection or '--' separator, leaving ping flag/argument injection open (e.g. a host value starting with '-'); this gap already existed pre-fix so nothing new is introduced.
